what_i_got_wrong: I ACCEPTED MY OWN INSTRUMENT'S SILENCE AS A MEASUREMENT FOR MOST OF AN HOUR. The cycle opened by running `health.py --check` with NO --gates-verdict and NO --stall-verdict, read `gates_green: NO-GATE-VERDICT ... bad for 46.5 h`, and carried that as a fact. It is an absent reading, not a reading of absence — CLAUDE.md §4, in the one file that exists to make that distinction. The real state was the opposite: CI had been measuring the row correctly the whole time and the board was simply never committed. I only caught it because the committed board and my local one disagreed, and I checked which was which instead of averaging them.

AND MY FIRST HYPOTHESIS FOR THE CAUSE WAS WRONG. I suspected `gates_verdict.py` was failing closed against the API. Running it (--dry-run, unauthenticated, from the sandbox) refuted that in one command: it returned a correct RED verdict. The discriminating observation cost nothing and was available before the hypothesis was.
